transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump says he rejected Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and
resume nuclear talks.
The offer comes as the two countries are deadlocked over how to end the conflict.
Iranian President Masoud Pajeskian tells CBS's Face the Nation that he's reluctant to meet
directly with Trump.
He's heard here through an interpreter.
The issue is now the atmosphere of distrust that has developed between Iran and the United
States is because we have had several rounds of talks with the United States.
We reached an agreement on the JCPOA and after months of negotiations, the U.S. president
tore it up.
Iran says it would allow U.N. nuclear inspectors into the country as part of a longer-term
ceasefire deal.
For now, there's no agreement to reopen the Strait or restart negotiations.
Hurricane Nolo is moving south of Hawaii.
Forecasters say the storm could bring up to two feet of rain to the Big Island, along
with dangerous flooding and mudslides.
NPR's Juliana Kim reports Nolo is the third hurricane to batter the state this year.
Big Island and Maui are expected to see heavy rain and strong winds this weekend.
While the other islands may be spared from Nolo's harshest impacts, the entire state
is reeling from months of natural disasters.
That includes major storms and an earthquake.
The state's governor, Josh Green, says over 1,200 homes have been damaged or destroyed
as a result.
He adds that recovery efforts will cost upwards of a billion dollars prior to Nolo.
Hurricane season in Hawaii is expected to last through November 30.
Juliana Kim, NPR News, Honolulu.
Forecasters expected to make landfall Monday with heavy rain that could cause flooding
and mudslides.
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a package of gun safety bills on Saturday.
Latchmi Sarah of member station KQED reports gun violence prevention advocates are praising
the move.
Ten new laws include one that funds intervention programs to interrupt violence and another
requiring that 3D printers sold in California block attempts to make ghost guns.
There's also one that creates a statewide office of violence prevention.
Mike McLively is the policy director of the Gifford Center for Violence Intervention.
There's a lot of state-level infrastructure now to support cities and community-based
organizations doing that violence intervention work, but we didn't have like a designated
office and this will now create a director of community violence intervention.
The California Rifle and Pistol Association opposed the bill on 3D printing guns, calling
it "a costly, impractical, and constitutionally problematic burden."
For NPR News, I'm Latchmi Sarah.
This is NPR.
The United States and China have agreed to set up a channel for handling incidents involving
artificial intelligence.
The agreement follows three days of talks between President Trump and Chinese President
Xi Jinping in Washington.
The two sides also plan to strengthen communication between their militaries during a crisis they're
set to meet again to discuss AI in November.
The U.S. has placed strict controls on microchips, semiconductors, and software-making equipment
in an effort to slow China's development.
Hollywood is writing an encore of "Avengers Endgame" to a surge in weekend attendance,
and PR's Bob Mondello reports superhero myths aren't the only ones proving to be durable
at the box office.
"Avengers Endgame" will have a brief burst of glory this weekend, wishing past $2.8 billion
worldwide, cementing its spot as the number two earner in box office history.
Tom Holland, one of its many stars, is also in "Spider-Man Brand New Day," which is approaching
$2.5 billion worldwide in spot number three.
And he's also in "Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey," a more traditional tale of mythic
heroes, which recently passed $1.7 billion and still sells out many of its weekend IMAX
performances before it's through.
This old-school sword-and-sandals epic with very few digital effects has a shot at cracking
the all-time worldwide top ten.
Bob Mondello, NPR News.
This is NPR News in Washington.
